setlist.title: Goin' Down The Road Feeling Bad

liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Franklin's Tower** (4 reviews): The Help>Slipknot>Franklin's sequence is the best this listener has heard, with Franklin's running over twenty minutes; Franklin's Tower is singled out as outstanding [2][5][6][13]
- **Scarlet Begonias** (3 reviews): Scarlet's transition into Goin' Down the Road is intriguing; the band audibly searches for a segue and succeeds; The Scarlet into Goin' Down the Road transition is called a unique, beautiful moment [3][9][12]
- **The Music Never Stopped** (2 reviews): Judged the best Music Never Stopped of the tour so far, closing a set of fast Big River and languid Loser; Music Never Stopped closes the first set with serious playing, then Bobby announces a break [8][11]
- **Help On The Way** (1 review): Help On the Way was played at a much peppier tempo than on the album [10]
- **New Minglewood Blues** (1 review): Minglewood after the roughly thirty-minute opening is perfunctory and ends abruptly [13]
- **Tennessee Jed** (1 review): Tennessee Jed follows at an up-tempo pace, with Jerry leading [13]
- **Not Fade Away Jam** (1 review): The Not Fade Away jam before Drums is described as unique [5]
- **Wharf Rat** (1 review): Wharf Rat is a highlight, with power, passion, soulful singing and guitar, and a tightly in-tune band [6]

## Setlist highlights

- **Not Fade Away Jam**: mythic rare: 2 archived performances [14]

## The recordings

- **gd77-04-29.moore.unknown.7113.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): audience recording; 23 songs; 198 min; rated 4.12/5 by 24 [1]. Said about its sound: Audience recording has some crowd noise, but it is mild and conveys the energy of the room [2]

## Around the show

- Reviewer mentions microdot and the band making small adjustments between songs without hurting the energy [8]
- Reviewer says Jerry plays with abundant ideas and high energy throughout the show [9]
- Reviewer attended this as a first show, sitting fifteenth row center at the Palladium [10]
- Show is less incendiary than others from the spring 1977 tour [3]
- Opening with the Help>Slipknot>Franklin suite is a change from many 1977 shows that begin with Promised Land [6]
- Slipknot is again the standout of the opening trio, as at the Springfield show [8]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd77-04-29.moore.unknown.7113.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Jerry Moore; source: Audience Recording: Sony ECM-33Ps [1]. Also: Reviewer's tape appears to be the same source as this one, but about five generations better; Recorded by Jerry Moore with Sony ECM-33P microphones and a Sony TC-158 deck; Transfer chain: audience master cassette to digital, then CDR, then SHN, obtained via CDead [1][5]
